newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says EU nations lodge Belarus protest.
newsitem.headline: France says EU nations lodge Belarus protest.

text.p: France said on Tuesday it had protested to Belarus, along with Germany, Britain and Italy against a referendum called by President Alexander Lukashenko in a bid to to increase his powers.
French foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters that ambassadors of the four European Union countries had delivered the protest in Minsk.

"We have expressed to Belarus authorities our concern at the illegal nature of this referendum following last week's events and the sacking of the president of the electoral commission," Rummelhardt said.

Western embassies in the Belarussian capital, including the French mission, said they were puzzled by the French statement, adding that there had been no fresh diplomatic approach by EU countries to Lukashenko's government for several weeks.

Lukashenko has called the vote next Sunday to amend the constitution and tighten his grip on rival institutions. He earlier fired the head of the independent election commission and ignored rulings by the constitutional court.

"France reasserts its desire that the Minsk authorities respect the essential values on which democracy is based," Rummelhardt said. "France hopes that all parties will reach a solution through dialogue and respect of the constitutional order."

In Bonn, a German foreign ministry spokesman said the four countries sent a joint note of protest to Minsk several days ago in the name of the European Union. "The constitution needs to be respected," he said.

However, Britain denied the EU had taken collective action. "There has been no joint approach," a foreign ministry spokesman said. In Rome, a foreign ministry official said Italy and other countries had individually expressed perplexity about the referendum on various occasions.
In Strasbourg, the parliamentary assembly of the Council of Europe said Lukashenko's moves could prevent Belarus membership of the 40-member body which promotes democracy and human rights.

"We fear that the constitutional crisis shaking Belarus may jeopardise that country's chances of joining the Council of Europe," said a statement by speaker Leni Fischer and the heads of the assembly's political groups.
The assembly urged Lukashenko to heed the constitutional council's November 4 ruling that the referendum should have no legal force.

Prime Minister Mikhail Chigir, who had remained loyal to Lukashenko during months of political paralysis, resigned on Monday. Lukashenko named deputy prime minister Sergei Ling as acting premier. Labour minister Alexander Sosnov also resigned.
Deputies have been occupying parliament around the clock since Friday to protest at Lukashenko's plans.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin called on Tuesday for compromise and common sense in neighbouring Belarus and said he was worried about the rise in tension there, the Kremlin said.
